substantive_actions.independent_reconstruction: Whole FY2026 DHS appropriation and bounded lapse-pay/obligation-ratification proposition. Direct retired/dependent care financing in a mixed $1.249-billion account; $123.5-million emergency food/shelter support with 3.5% administration cap; $684-million split firefighter/staffing grants with existing clinical/EMS uses and permissive named waivers; incorporated January allocations for child/workforce care and medical-information systems. Qualified custody treatment, prescription-import funding limits, Federal DHS license portability through September 30, 2026 and discretionary backup care coexist with wider security/enforcement/transportation spending. Passed 221–209 with two Not Voting; Foushee Nay / Massie Yea.
substantive_actions.health_membership_basis: Actual care financing/custody-care governance and direct food/shelter assistance, not DHS label.
substantive_actions.yea_nay_audit: Yea supports and Nay opposes this exact proposition; no preferred alternative, motive or component position inferred.
substantive_actions.qualification_audit: Whole-package choice, not component positions or medical-only spending. Statement allocations are within accounts. Final $8.911-million information-exchange allocation supersedes report $8.113-million proposal. CBP policy retains populations, welfare checks, resources/operational distinctions and no private action; alternative is qualified. Pregnancy exceptions do not automatically extend to post-delivery recuperation; labor/delivery prohibition is categorical. Import rule retains FDA compliance, on-person 90-day/personal-use and exclusions. Licensed practice stays within Federal duties with Coast Guard exclusions. Pay authority already exists; only bounded lawful obligations ratified. No enactment, compliance or outcome inference.
